title: Design the Decision Process
goals: Design a decision process that covers valid, invalid and no-match requests
Trace changing state and explain why the search stops
Preserve both compatibility conditions and the agreed first-match rule
vocabulary: Checking an input against the agreed rules before using it
A path chosen according to a condition
Information that records the process’s current position or values
Reaching a point where the process stops

worked_example.title: Trace a request before trusting the design

headers: Stage for 9 minutes and Quiet required No
rows: 9 is a whole number in range; No is valid
8 is no more than 9; quiet is not required

blocks.text: The current candidate changes from B1 to B2. The request values stay the same. After B2 passes, the process stops: it does not replace B2 with a later fitting row. This early stop preserves the first-match rule and gives the same required suggestion as the manual baseline, which marked every row before selecting the first fit.

Termination needs a reason. There are only four rows, each failed check moves to the next row, and no row is revisited. A valid request therefore examines at most four candidates. A success can stop sooner. Invalid input stops before the search. Merely drawing an arrow around a loop is not enough; the state must make progress toward an end.

guided_practice.title: Track the current candidate
guided_practice.prompt: Trace 9 minutes with Quiet required No. Record the current candidate, time result, quiet condition and next step until the process stops. Explain why the request values should not change as the candidate advances.
guided_practice.answer: B1 fails time because 10 is greater than 9; quiet is unrestricted. Advance to B2. B2 passes time because 8 is no more than 9 and quiet is not required, so suggest B2 and stop. Candidate state changes to search the catalogue; changing the request values would solve a different task.

independent_case.title: Design a complete room decision process
independent_case.task: A new paper catalogue lists C1 first, capacity 4, quiet Yes; C2 second, capacity 8, quiet No. Valid requests give a whole group size from 1 to 10 and Quiet required Yes or No. A room fits if capacity is at least group size and the quiet condition is met; choose the first fit. Write a complete process with validation, search, state change and stopping rules. Trace 6 people No and explain the outcome for a blank quiet field. No booking takes place.
independent_case.answer: Validate group size and Yes or No; request clarification and stop if invalid. Start C1; check capacity and quiet. If both pass, suggest and stop; otherwise advance to C2. If C2 also fails, report no match and stop. For 6 No, C1 fails capacity, C2 passes capacity with quiet unrestricted, so suggest C2. Blank quiet requires clarification before searching. Each failed row advances, so at most two candidates are checked.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: One failed row proves no match
Later rows may fit; continue until a fit or catalogue exhaustion.
The time and quiet conditions must both hold.
Any compatible answer satisfies the task
The first-in-catalogue tie rule is also a requirement.
A loop stops because it should
Show a state change that advances toward a finite end.

blocks.text: INPUT  approved input fields
PROCESS  smallest rule or learned decision flow with visible branches
OUTPUT  suggested bin, not sure, and reason
CORE IDEA  Rules or learned patterns must connect inputs to outputs transparently.

UNDER THE HOOD  A decision process operationalizes the interface contract. Simplicity improves testability and explanation, but oversimplification can erase relevant distinctions. Learned components need explicit data, threshold, and fallback documentation.
Draw a fresh example with all three stages:
A closer explanation

blocks.title: Four paths through the recommender
blocks.caption: Failing one candidate continues the search. No match is justified only after the valid request has no fitting candidate.

blocks.text: Begin by checking the request. If minutes are missing, outside 0 to 30 or not a whole number, ask for a whole number in that range. If the quiet field is not Yes or No, ask for one of those values. State the fields needing correction and stop this run. When a corrected request arrives, validate it as a new run rather than continuing with old candidate state.

For a valid request, start at B1. Check time and the quiet condition for the current candidate. If both pass, output that candidate and stop. If either fails, move forward exactly one row. After B4 fails, there is no next row, so output no match and stop. Never jump back to B1 within the same search.

CASE 2 — Learned classifier  Clue: patterns from examples. Meaning: needs data evidence.
CASE 3 — Extra unused field  Clue: never changes path. Meaning: remove.
CASE 4 — No fallback  Clue: forces ambiguous label. Meaning: add review.
BOUNDARY  Transparent does not mean correct; the flow still needs testing.
